svg.text: 19 packings above n = 324 that improve the Squares Project record
Before: Squares Project record on 17 October 2026 (published packing or integer grid). After: strongest selected solution.
Reused published packings and components are identified below each pair.
Solutions generated by GPT-6 Astra through numerical search and refinement, working with Joost de Winter.
This SVG, including its layout, drawings and brief explanations, was generated by GPT-6 Astra.
GPT-6 Astra may make mistakes in its self-assessments of how it arrived at a solution.
Same square size within each pair.

g.text: Shared construction method for the following 19 packings
These packings use the staircase-rectangle and four-block method of Arslanov, Mustafin and Shangitbayev (2021).
GPT-6 Astra searched component variants and assemblies, then numerically refined the resulting packings.
A six-square patch from n=422 was transferred into the n=464 construction. The resulting interface was refined, then used as a donor for the n=382
The replacement alters the tilted/upright interface; two previously upright squares become tilted.
The left panel is the packing the Squares Project holds: Francisco Couzo's certificate of 14 October 2026.
Two compressed tilted components (118 and 110 squares) and two aligned grids form 118 + 110 + 225 + 56 = 509. GPT-6 Astra searched component
variants, assembled them with the grids, and refined the complete packing.
Staggered joins between the tilted components and aligned grids allow 509 squares within s < 23. The left panel is an exact integer-grid
Two compressed tilted components (125 and 118 squares) and two aligned grids form 125 + 118 + 256 + 56 = 555. GPT-6 Astra searched component
variants, assembled them with the grids, and refined the complete packing. Latest pass: an interface angle deformation followed by relaxation
